en.title: The Letters Î and Â
en.summary: Learn how to pronounce the letters î and â with the same vowel sound.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Two letters write the same sound in this language. A letter is a written sign of the alphabet. This sound is a vowel. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. Your tongue stays in the middle of your mouth. You hear this vowel in (români) /roˈmɨnʲ/.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Do not round your lips. Your lips stay flat. Move your tongue toward the middle of your mouth. Keep your tongue high inside your mouth. Touch your throat and feel it shake. Push air through your mouth. You make this sound in (români) /roˈmɨnʲ/.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Both letters make the exact same sound. You write â inside words most of the time. You see this letter inside (români) /roˈmɨnʲ/. You write î at the start of words. You also write î at the end of words. You also find î inside some words. Both letters always make the exact same vowel.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make two different sounds for these letters. They sound the same every time. Do not move your tongue forward. If you move your tongue forward, you say 'see'. Do not round your lips. If you round your lips, you say 'too'. Keep your lips flat when you say (români) /roˈmɨnʲ/.
